say.en: Air is 78 percent nitrogen, yet nitrogen is the element crops most often lack. Its triple bond is so strong that only a few microbes, lightning and factories can break it. In this lesson: Describe the nitrogen cycle.
Explain biological nitrogen fixation and root nodule formation.
Describe how plants make amino acids from ammonia.

body.en: *Nitrogen* fixation turns N₂ into ammonia (by microbes, lightning and industry). Ammonification releases ammonia from dead matter. Nitrification oxidises ammonia to nitrite (Nitrosomonas, Nitrococcus) and then nitrate (Nitrobacter). Plants absorb nitrate and ammonium. Denitrification by bacteria such as Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus returns N₂ to the air. Free-living fixers include Azotobacter and Beijernickia (aerobic), Rhodospirillum (anaerobic) and cyanobacteria such as Anabaena and Nostoc; Rhizobium fixes nitrogen in legume root nodules.

Nitrification oxidises ammonia to nitrite (Nitrosomonas, Nitrococcus) and then nitrate Nitrobacter. Plants absorb nitrate and ammonium. Fixation gives ammonification gives nitrification gives uptake.
Denitrification returns N 2.
Nitrogenase is found only in prokaryotes.

problem.en: Why are root nodules of an actively fixing legume pink inside, and why does a pea crop enrich the soil?

steps.en: The pink colour is leghaemoglobin, which keeps oxygen low for nitrogenase.
Rhizobium in the nodules fixes N₂ into ammonia, part of which the plant uses.
When roots and nodules decay, the fixed nitrogen is added to the soil.

answer.en: Leghaemoglobin; nodules add fixed nitrogen to the soil

prompt.en: Put the steps of root nodule formation in order.

steps.en: Roots secrete chemicals that attract Rhizobium.
Rhizobia multiply and attach to the root hair, which curls.
An infection thread carries the bacteria into the cortex.
Cortical and pericycle cells divide to form the nodule.
Bacteria are released, become bacteroids and fix nitrogen.
Vascular connections let the nodule exchange nutrients with the plant.

points.en: Nitrogen cycle: fixation, ammonification, nitrification, uptake, denitrification.
Nitrogenase (prokaryotes only) needs ATP and an oxygen-free site; leghaemoglobin protects it in nodules.
Ammonia becomes amino acids by reductive amination and transamination; amides carry nitrogen.
